title: The Day of the Grand Exit
skyStory: Last quarter, sixty-seven percent lit, and the moon is taking its final bows in Leo. Last quarter is the moon's clearing-out phase: it sheds a little light every night like a performer removing glitter after a show. Leo insists on one more curtain call anyway. The audience, mostly seagulls and a fox, applauds politely. Tomorrow it will be backstage, tidying.

reading: The Tiger has been carrying something for weeks that it no longer needs: an old plan, a project that fizzled, a should that belongs to someone else. Today you can set it down, take a bow and walk off stage left. No farewell speech necessary. The [[Eight of Swords]] was only ever a cage made of thoughts.

Make a tiny ceremony of it. Write the thing on a scrap of paper, fold it twice and drop it in the woodstove or the recycling, whichever feels more theatrical. Then do one thing that makes you feel light: a walk at dusk, a song turned up loud, a long look at the stars. Notice how much more room there is in the cabin.
joel.mission: Recycle or give away three things today, and narrate each farewell like a sports commentator.
joel.omen: A leaf letting go of a branch in still air. Letting go can be graceful, quiet and entirely voluntary.
joel.elementWhy: burn off what you no longer need

reading: The Wood Rat is a collector by nature, and somewhere in the nest is a pile of things kept just in case. Today one of those things gets to leave. You will know which one: it will feel lighter the moment you decide. The nest will feel roomier by bedtime.

Last quarter moons love a clear-out, and Leo wants it done with flair. Hold the object up, tell it one story about why you kept it, thank it and let it go. The hollow wish of the [[Nine of Cups]] loosens its grip a little every time you choose what you actually want over what you thought you should want.
nancy.mission: Choose one thing kept just in case and give it a proper send-off speech before it leaves.
nancy.omen: An empty shelf catching the afternoon light. Space is a gift, and you just gave it to yourself.

together.text: Each of you name one thing you are leaving behind in November. Say it once, out loud or in a message, then never mention it again this year. Replace it with one word you want to carry into December. Nancy's birthday month is coming, and it deserves a clean stage.
